An **agent trace** is a record of an agent’s execution. Depending on the framework and settings, it can show the input, steps or events, tool calls and their results, and the agent’s final output. Traces help people inspect and debug behavior. They record observable execution; they are **not necessarily a transcript of the model’s private reasoning**.

**Example:** A user asks, “What’s the weather in Paris?” The trace shows the question arriving, the agent calling a weather tool, the tool returning current conditions, and the agent replying with the result.

The term varies across tools: LangSmith represents traces as related runs, OpenAI’s Agents SDK records workflow events such as tool calls and handoffs, and OpenTelemetry uses traces made up of spans to represent work across a system.

**References:** [LangSmith observability concepts](https://docs.smith.langchain.com/observability/concepts), [OpenAI Agents SDK tracing](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing/), [OpenTelemetry traces](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/traces/).
